documents.name: Spring Economic Update 2026 (Canada Strong for All)

next: Read through Budget 2026, tabled 5 November 2026; the list will be refreshed after the next fiscal update.

items.text: $55.2 million over four years to Transport Canada for safety-related infrastructure at local and regional airports through the Airports Capital Assistance Program, including a priority project to extend the runway at the Transport Canada-owned Îles-de-la-Madeleine Airport (program-wide amount; the runway's share is not stated).
Supporting Medical School Infrastructure: funding for Toronto Metropolitan University's School of Medicine campus in Brampton ($25 million in 2027-28).
$9 million over three years to Environment and Climate Change Canada to support the Biosphère in Montréal.
$100 million for federal activities (Canadian Heritage, RCMP, CBSA, IRCC, CATSA, CFIA) supporting the hosting of the FIFA Men's World Cup 2026 in Toronto and Vancouver.
Support for Cape Breton Operations in managing legacy liabilities (Public Services and Procurement Canada), $18 million over five years (Annex 1, Table A1.18).

$5 billion Trade Diversification Corridors Fund (Transport Canada). Named examples: the Port of Saguenay's second wharf, container designation at Québec City and Hamilton, rail lines in Alberta, West Coast port and rail. No per-project amounts.
Darlington New Nuclear Project in Bowmanville: $2 billion investment from the Canada Growth Fund, plus $1 billion from Ontario.
Large Enterprise Tariff Loan to Algoma Steel (Sault Ste. Marie): access to $400 million in liquidity, with Ontario adding $100 million.
Build Canada Homes: a request for qualifications for 540 new homes at Arbo Downsview in Toronto.
The new preclearance facility at Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport, for which the government invested $30 million in 2023.
The new B Jetty at CFB Esquimalt created close to 1,300 jobs; the River-class Destroyer project is expected to create or maintain over 5,000 jobs over 15 years, many in Halifax.

items.text: Major Projects Office referral: Mackenzie Valley Highway, Wrigley to Inuvik.

Mackenzie Valley Highway: Budget 2026 proposes to fully fund construction and certain maintenance of the ~800 km all-season highway from Wrigley to the Dempster Highway south of Inuvik, passing near Tulita, Norman Wells and Fort Good Hope ($3.1 billion over five years in the Chapter 2 table).
items.department: Major projects (department not named in the table)

items.text: $187.4 million over five years (and $24.2 million in future years) to launch a major projects management entity and begin support for the Mackenzie Valley Highway and the Taltson Hydro Expansion project (entity-wide amount; Taltson's share is not stated).
items.department: Privy Council Office / Major Projects Office

items.text: Grays Bay Road and Port: highlighted as the northern mineral corridor the government is advancing; no federal amount stated in the budget text.
Roberts Bank Terminal 2: the proposed three-berth container terminal adding about 50% to the Port of Vancouver's container capacity; no federal amount stated.
Deep Geological Repository for used nuclear fuel (Ignace area, northwestern Ontario): highlighted as a major project; no federal amount stated.
Red Chris Mine extension, northwestern British Columbia: federal contribution of $500 million announced in July 2026 (copper; about 1,500 jobs in operation).
Darlington New Nuclear Project: an approximately $715 million federal-provincial loan guarantee lets seven Williams Treaties First Nations take a minority stake.
items.department: Indigenous Loan Guarantee Program (Canada Development Investment Corporation)

items.text: Teck Resources' $850 million expansion of its Trail Operations: first agreement under the $2 billion Canada Critical Minerals Accelerator, alongside a $400 million Canada Growth Fund investment.
items.department: Export Development Canada / Canada Growth Fund

items.text: Up to $2.5 billion in Export Development Canada financing to De Havilland to expand waterbomber production in Wheatland County, Alberta.

Ending homelessness in Winnipeg with Manitoba: over $1 billion in new capital through Build Canada Homes, including up to $800 million for 2,000 transitional and permanent supportive units and the Winnipeg Centre for Mental Health and Addictions.
Brandon, Manitoba: $42.8 million Canada Infrastructure Bank investment in water and wastewater infrastructure for about 2,300 new homes.
Whitehorse, Yukon: $19.8 million supporting Kwanlin Dün First Nation with roads, water and utilities on its settlement lands for more than 380 new homes.
Toronto and Mississauga: a $600 million investment expanding low-carbon district energy systems.
RCMP Heritage Centre, Regina: designated a national museum, with access to $3 million a year up to 2029-30 for the transition.
$15.9 million over four years to Veterans Affairs Canada to acquire, remediate and operate the National Field of Honour (Pointe-Claire).

Ferry Services Contribution Program renewed to 2032 ($1.3 billion over eight years), including new terminals at Wood Islands (PEI) and Caribou (NS) and interim replacement vessels (program-wide amount).
VIA Rail: more than $6.6 billion for new passenger cars and locomotives (announced September 2026), designed in Saint-Bruno-de-Montarville and built in Thunder Bay and La Pocatière.
LaSalle Causeway Bridge Replacement and Renewal Project in Kingston, using $261.8 million of existing funding.
Tla'amin Nation acquiring 100% of Western Forest Products' Stillwater Forest Operation, backed by the Indigenous Loan Guarantee Program.
Nearly $2 billion for 190 Armoured Combat Support Vehicles, assembled at the General Dynamics Land Systems–Canada plant in London, Ontario.
Agreement with Chantier Davie to build six program icebreakers for the Canadian Coast Guard (about 5,000 construction jobs); amount not stated.
items.department: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (Canadian Coast Guard)

items.text: Wainwright: $25 million over two years for Canadian Forces Morale and Welfare Services after the tragedy at CFB Wainwright, plus $3 million for the Wainwright Military Family Resource Centre.

Completing a General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems nitrocellulose production facility in Québec (placed at the company's Valleyfield plant), funded from the $2.7 billion defence industrial base envelope.
Canada's $150 million share (with Germany's €100 million) in Montréal-based LawZero, the AI safety lab founded by Yoshua Bengio.
